hook_formula: High-concept absurd premise delivered instantly ('Every time I talked to my crush, something falls from the sky') paired with an immediate visual gag (a piano crashing down), stopping the scroll by creating instant narrative curiosity and dark comedy.
story_arc: Setup: Protagonist introduces the curse where objects fall from the sky when talking to his crush. Escalation: Objects get progressively bigger (flower pot, bathtub, piano, canoe, shopping cart) as he tries helmets and friends. Clue discovery: He notices a tiny bell and scratch marks. Twist/Payoff: He confesses anyway, looks up, and discovers her cat has been maliciously pushing objects off the roof all year; the cat drops a single rose instead of a car to seal the romance.

source_transcript: Every time I talked to my crush, something falls from the sky. Yesterday it was a piano. It started small. Hi! Gotta flower pot. Can I borrow a pencil? Gotta bathtub. Then we talked about homework for one whole minute. That was the piano. She never ran away. I almost did. The longer I talked, the bigger it gets. And I still haven't asked her out. I tried wearing three helmets. I sent my best friend to ask for me. A canoe landed on him. I called her from my bedroom. A shopping cart came through my ceiling. Two things bugged me. Right before every crash I heard a tiny bell. And everything that fell had scratch marks on it. So today I went to her house and asked anyway. Will you go out with? I heard the bell. I looked up. Her cat was on the roof pushing a car toward the edge. It had been the cat all year. She looked up too. Don't! She told the cat. I'm saying yes. The cat stared at me for a long time. Then it pushed something off the roof anyway. A rose.
